chemicals.concentration_notes: These toxic compounds are found throughout the plant, including the flowers, leaves, bark, and roots. Poisoning can be severe and potentially fatal; death has been reported in animals.
chemicals.description: Brunfelsamidine is a central nervous system stimulant that causes excitement, tremors, and tonic-clonic seizures, while hopeanine acts as a depressant. The mechanism is strychnine-like, interfering with inhibitory (glycine) neurotransmission. Signs can be biphasic, alternating excitation with depression.
chemicals.name: Brunfelsamidine and hopeanine

description:
Yesterday-Today-and-Tomorrow (Brunfelsia pauciflora) is a flowering shrub known for its blossoms that change color from purple to white over several days. All parts of this plant are toxic to cats and can cause serious neurological and gastrointestinal symptoms if ingested.

The plant contains several toxic compounds, including brunfelsamidine, which affects the central nervous system. Ingestion can lead to a dangerous combination of effects, often starting with stimulation (agitation, tremors) and progressing to depression (lethargy, and in severe cases, coma).

Signs of poisoning include vomiting, drooling, muscle tremors, loss of coordination, and seizures. The alternating periods of agitation and sedation are a characteristic sign. Because the neurological symptoms can escalate quickly, any suspected ingestion should be treated as a medical emergency. Please contact a veterinarian immediately if you think your cat has chewed on this plant.
emergencyNote: Administration of Respiratory and Cardiac Stimulants
name: Yesterday-today-and-tomorrow
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: brunfelsamidine (a stimulant) and hopeanine (a depressant); all parts of the plant are toxic
Mechanism: brunfelsamidine acts on the central nervous system in a strychnine-like manner, interfering with inhibitory neurotransmission and producing excitation, while hopeanine produces depression
Symptoms: vomiting, diarrhea, muscle tremors, seizures; characteristically produces a syndrome that alternates agitation with sedation
Frequently used as a decorative garden shrub in tropical regions — keep cats away from the garden
Seek veterinary care promptly if ingestion is suspected; the neurological syndrome can escalate rapidly

symptoms.name: Vomiting
symptoms.notes: Vomiting is one of the gastrointestinal signs documented after ingestion of Brunfelsia by cats.

symptoms.name: Drooling (hypersalivation)
symptoms.notes: Excessive salivation is documented in Brunfelsia poisoning by ASPCA and veterinary toxicology sources.

symptoms.name: Diarrhea
symptoms.notes: Diarrhea is listed by ASPCA among the gastrointestinal signs of Brunfelsia ingestion.

symptoms.name: Ataxia (loss of coordination) and tremors
symptoms.notes: These symptoms highlight the severe neurological disruption caused by the plant's toxic compounds.

symptoms.name: Seizures
symptoms.notes: Brunfelsamidine produces tonic-clonic seizures; ASPCA reports seizures that may persist for several days.

symptoms.name: Depression, deep sedation, and sometimes coma
symptoms.notes: Poisoning can lead to a profound comatose state requiring respiratory support and intensive supportive treatment. Toxicosis is severe and potentially fatal; deaths have been reported in animals.

treatments.description: The veterinarian administers specific stimulant medications to support and revive the cat's cardiovascular and respiratory systems.
treatments.name: Administration of Respiratory and Cardiac Stimulants
treatments.notes: This is the most urgent intervention and is specifically recommended if the cat has become severely depressed, heavily sedated, or has slipped into a coma as a result of the poisoning.

treatments.description: The veterinary team provides ongoing symptom management and monitoring to stabilize the cat until the toxins clear its system.
treatments.name: General Supportive Care
treatments.notes: Because the plant can cause a wide variety of systemic issues—such as an abnormally fast heart rate (tachycardia), urinary retention, tremors, and loss of coordination (ataxia)—supportive care is essential and will be tailored to the specific symptoms the cat is actively experiencing.
